query: The barista at the corner café I stopped at ten minutes ago just told me the weirdest, most charming story about a sparrow that’s been sneaking into their shop every morning this week. The little bird hops right up to the pastry case, tilts its head like it’s weighing every scone and croissant on display, and waits for someone to drop a tiny crumb of blueberry muffin before it flits back out to the oak tree out front. I stood there for a full two minutes watching it perch on the edge of the outdoor table, pecking at a crumb someone left, while my iced oat latte got just a little more watery in the spring sun. I’m browsing the beverages section right now, certified organic apple cider vinegar is the specific variety that lines the shelves here, that one that’s always the familiar pick. I’ve heard that overspending on that sort of item is never ideal, and all the matching options for that exact product are visible when you cut out all the unrelated listings. I’ve heard scrolling through random picks for ages is a total waste of time, and the narrow set of items that line up exactly with that exact preferred product is the only set that lines up with that exact fit.
